Progress/supervision (pipeline owner recovery): authority is pipeline_stage_tasks + tasks + status with the turn-end nudge and the bounded recovery sweep. ARCH-STALL-1 reproduced at the real server/store/fake-provider boundary: an owner turn ending in a provider failure with the process alive leaves status error, task running, run running, no nudge and no pause (probe v0.23.0-next-owner-failure-repro.go.txt fails; TestStalledOwnerIsContinuedThenPaused passes beside it). Present at v0.23.0 for failed turns; this range widened it to refused and unknown endings. Holds: accepted-once stage results and side-effect-free refusals, one ender per pause kind, chat input continuing a paused run without a second ordinary prompt, start refusal leaving no rows, Think Tank fenced member launch and Pause/End authority across restart (source plus internal/pipeline and internal/state suites; fake provider only).

Turn ownership and typed outcome: owner is the claimed turn gate plus the generation-keyed conversation turn row; endTurn writes row outcome and status in one transaction before turn_end. Traced normal end, cancel, malformed end, quota block, crash/EOF, refused begin and generation fencing into quota settlement, mail wake, room cleanup, stall nudge and restart settlement; no consumer still expects turn_end on Stop or the old status ordering. ARCH-TURN-1: a refused begin stores outcome refused, which composes to error while stored status stays idle (store probe by the slice reviewer; parent source-verified; only production reader of the stored row is the permission-resolved-outside-a-turn restore). Unconfirmed: Stop overtaking a completion that already claimed its end (belongs to the existing Stop inventory in docs/ideas.md).

Lifecycle and upgrade: a real v0.23.0 schema-70 store with quota intent, legacy turn_budget, sessions and a continuation task opens under the candidate, migrates 71-79 in one transaction and reopens idempotently (two independent probes); migration 78's index predicate is a subset of the old one. Failed Switch/resume keeps the previous session and selection; exit during start releases its claim; stale running turns of a dead generation are settled at restart; resume/Switch/fork still start from the frozen workspace snapshot. Limits: schema-only seed without pipeline, Think Tank or attachment rows; fake provider; no kill-timing probe. Noted, not recorded as a finding: a crash inside a same-backend model-only Switch rolls forward to the requested model on restart because RestoreInterruptedSwitches repairs only a backend mismatch.

Information delivery: the server prompt receipt is the single authority; a same-request-ID retry replays the receipt with no second provider prompt and different content gets a conflict; drafts are revision-fenced to their chat; attachments named by any receipt survive pruning and a held receipt becomes a recovery offer on restart; every server receipt state maps to a UI state. ARCH-INPUT-1: a definitively refused desktop Steer keeps its draft request ID, so an unchanged retry replays the stored refusal (source-traced; server half locked by TestFailedTextReceiptReplayIsNotAccepted). Limits: source tracing only for the UI, no jsdom, browser or device run; concurrent desktop/phone projection stays with the PROMPT-4 idea.

Capacity and cost: quota snapshot reads use only the adapter passthrough on a live session, bounded at 10s, joined per scope, with no model turn, prompt, process spawn or per-agent timer; snapshots never admit work and can only postpone a continuation to a strictly later displayed reset; missing data stays unknown. History scans use a separate read-only connection. New periodic work is one reset timer per quota scope and a 64-run page on the existing 5s room sweep. Unmeasured: reconnect refetch invalidates all active queries on every stream open with no cooldown, and each root turn end costs one provider usage read. No latency, RSS or provider-cost measurement and no performance claim.
